name: Gathering baselining information to inform a local plan
fact: MHCLG guidance updated 26 March 2026 recommends collecting, mapping and analysing current/future data, including transport, infrastructure, utilities and planning constraints, before Gateway 1.
gate: Baselining is early plan evidence; mapped opportunities or constraints are not site allocation, permission or parcel-level development readiness.

name: Preparing a local plan vision
fact: Updated 26 March 2026; local plans must include a vision and up to 10 measurable outcomes informed by baseline evidence and realistic delivery expectations.
gate: Vision and outcomes express plan ambition; they do not create a site allocation or permission.

name: Creating a plan timetable
fact: Updated 30 June 2026; planning authorities must publish and keep plan timetables current, including key milestone dates and standardised plan/timetable datasets.
gate: Timetable milestones are process evidence only; they do not establish site status or adoption.

name: Giving notice of your plan-making
fact: Updated 10 June 2026; notice to commence must be published before the 30-month preparation process and at least four months before Gateway 1.
gate: Notice to commence starts a plan-making pathway; it is not evidence that any site is allocated or permissioned.

name: Issue a requirement to assist notice
fact: Published 22 April 2026; LPAs may issue a requirement-to-assist notice to prescribed public bodies when essential plan-making information has not been supplied after routine requests.
gate: A request for infrastructure or public-body information is not itself capacity evidence and may still receive no usable site-level data.

name: Engaging the public when preparing a local plan
fact: Published 15 April 2026; guidance covers community and consultation-body engagement through proposed-content, proposed-plan and examination stages.
gate: Consultation activity does not imply plan adoption, allocation or consent.

name: Making local plan documents publicly available
fact: Published 16 April 2026; authorities must make specified plan documents publicly available online and for inspection, with machine-readable/searchable publication encouraged.
gate: Publication improves transparency but does not prove a document is adopted, current or determinative for a parcel.

name: Getting ready to prepare a new plan
fact: Updated 26 March 2026; pre-Gateway-1 readiness covers timetable, governance, consultation, anticipated plan content and Strategic Environmental Assessment preparation.
gate: Readiness is authority-level process evidence; no site allocation or deliverability is inferred.

name: Rollout of the new local plan-making system
fact: Updated 6 March 2026; new local-plan regulations came into force 25 March 2026, with transition rules and deadlines for authorities moving from the legacy system.
gate: System rollout dates do not establish the legal status of an individual emerging site or policy.

name: Procedure guide for new local plan system published
fact: Planning Inspectorate news published 24 June 2026 confirms the initial procedure guide for the 2026 gateway and examination system and notes legacy/new systems run together during 2026.
gate: A procedure-guide publication is process evidence, not site-level planning status.

name: Planning Inspectorate legacy local plans guidance collection
fact: Collection updated 20 July 2026; it applies to legacy-system plans submitted for examination on or before 31 December 2026.
gate: Legacy guidance applicability must be matched to the exact plan route and submission date.

name: Publish your plan data detailed standard
fact: Updated 13 May 2026; the approved standard requires separate plan and plan-timetable datasets and standardised publication for new-system local, minerals/waste and supplementary plans.
gate: Standardised publication improves machine readability but does not prove the published plan data is adopted or site-specific.

name: Plan and plan timetable template
fact: Updated 13 May 2026; MHCLG provides CSV templates for plan and plan-timetable data under the Planning Data (England) Regulations 2026.
gate: Template compliance is a data-quality aid, not evidence of plan adoption or development consent.

name: NSIP advice for local authorities
fact: Planning Inspectorate advice updated 14 July 2026 explains local-authority roles in the NSIP process and points users to national infrastructure planning guidance.
gate: Local-authority participation in an NSIP process does not prove the project will receive a DCO or create parcel uplift.

name: NSIP advice for submitting representations or comments
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; advice covers relevant representations, comments, redaction and examination-library participation for NSIPs.
gate: A representation or interested-party status is process evidence, not a development outcome.

name: NSIP EIA notification and consultation advice
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; advice explains notification and consultation of prescribed bodies on Environmental Statement scope for NSIPs.
gate: Scoping/consultation does not establish environmental acceptability or DCO approval.

name: NSIP application documents preparation advice
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; advice covers application form, Environmental Statement, HRA, plans, GIS shapefile, draft DCO, file indexing and submission standards.
gate: A well-formed submission can still be refused; document readiness is not development consent.

name: NSIP advice on good design
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; PINS advice sets out how good design should be considered for NSIP applications.
gate: Design guidance is qualitative process evidence and does not create permission or economic uplift.

name: NSIP rights of entry to land advice
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; advice explains section 53 rights-of-entry authorisation for land potentially affected by an NSIP.
gate: A right-to-enter process is not evidence of land acquisition, DCO grant or final project boundary.

name: NSIP consultation report advice
fact: Updated 14 July 2026; advice explains how applicants should compile and evidence statutory/non-statutory consultation in the consultation report.
gate: Consultation completion is not equivalent to acceptance, examination success or DCO grant.

name: Planning Act 2008 decision-making stage guidance
fact: Published 3 July 2026 as part of the refreshed National Infrastructure Planning Guidance suite; the portal states the July 2026 suite replaces prior guidance from 24 July 2026.
gate: Current date is 23 July 2026; do not treat this replacement guidance as having superseded the prior suite one day early.

name: Planning Act 2008 acceptance stage guidance
fact: Published 3 July 2026; guidance explains acceptance requirements, publicity and relevant-representation timing for DCO applications.
gate: The refreshed suite is stated to replace prior guidance from 24 July 2026; today is 23 July, and acceptance is not consent.

name: Planning Act 2008 examination stage guidance
fact: Published 3 July 2026; guidance sets out examination principles, timetable, written representations and hearings for DCO applications.
gate: Do not apply the replacement status before 24 July 2026; examination activity is not a DCO grant.

name: Planning Act 2008 pre-application steps guidance
fact: Published 3 July 2026; pre-application guidance covers programme management, engagement and key application-preparation considerations, including NSIP BNG from 2 November 2026.
gate: Today is 23 July 2026; preserve both the 24 July replacement date and 2 November 2026 BNG commencement date.

name: Planning Act 2008 application contents guidance
fact: Published 3 July 2026; guidance lists statutory DCO application content, plans, compulsory-acquisition information and digital/GIS submission expectations.
gate: Complete application contents do not prove acceptance or DCO approval; replacement status is not applied before 24 July 2026.

name: Planning Act 2008 infrastructure planning fees guidance July 2026
fact: Published 3 July 2026; statutory guidance covers cost recovery for specified public authorities and PINS pre-application services under the Infrastructure Planning Fees Regulations.
gate: Fees and service levels are process-cost evidence, not project viability or consent evidence.

name: National Infrastructure Planning Guidance Portal
fact: The portal states the new July 2026 NSIP guidance was published 3 July and will replace listed prior guidance from 24 July 2026.
gate: Current date is 23 July 2026; this portal is the controlling evidence for not applying the replacement one day early.
